About us
Danieli Morgårdshammar AB is part of the international Danieli Group and has been serving the Nordic metals industry for more than 170 years. Based in Smedjebacken, Sweden, we support steel, aluminum and other metal producers throughout Scandinavia with engineering services, spare parts, technical support and long-term partnership solutions.

We operate in an industry where trust, competence and personal relationships are often more important than presentations, marketing materials or corporate references. Our success is built on credibility and on being recognized as a reliable partner by the people who operate and maintain production facilities every day.
 
Responsibilities
We are looking for an experienced industry professional who already understands the reality of steel mills, rolling mills and metal processing plants.
This is not a typical sales position, more a business developer position.
The ideal candidate is someone who has worked directly within the metals industry or closely alongside plant personnel and understands how industrial decisions are truly made. Candidates coming directly from steel, aluminum or other metals production facilities are particularly encouraged to apply.
The primary focus of this role is the development of Danieli aftermarket and service business.
Activities include the sales, coordination, and follow-up of the following services and solutions for your designated customers:
Spare Parts Supply
Technical Services
On-site Assistance
Maintenance Support
Roll Shop Solutions
Equipment Refurbishments
Small and Medium Revamping Projects
Plant Modernizations and Upgrades
Engineering and Technical Consulting

Success in this role requires the ability to understand customers' operational challenges and identify opportunities where Danieli's technical expertise and service capabilities can create measurable value.
Technical Requirements
We are particularly interested in candidates who have:
Previous experience in the steel, aluminum or metals industry.
Direct experience working in or closely with production plants, rolling mills, maintenance organizations or technical departments.
Existing professional relationships within the Nordic metals industry.
A strong understanding of industrial operations, maintenance and production environments.
Experience interacting with: Roll Shop Managers; Production Managers; Maintenance Managers; Foremen and Supervisors; Category Managers; Purchasing Departments; Technical Specialists.

More than technical qualifications, we are looking for someone who understands plant culture, speaks the language of industrial operations and can quickly establish credibility with the people who influence purchasing decisions.
Fluent English, written and spoken, mother language Swedish.
Willingness to travel throughout the Nordic countries.
Valid driving license.
Experience with CRM systems (but not as a primary focus)
Technical education or equivalent industry experience is considered an advantage.

Soft Skills
For this position, interpersonal capabilities are just as important as technical knowledge.
The successful candidate will:
Build trust naturally and quickly.
Be highly relationship-driven and people-oriented.
Communicate confidently with personnel at all organizational levels.
Be proactive, decisive and commercially minded.
Feel comfortable opening doors and creating opportunities from scratch.
Demonstrate strong ownership and initiative.
Possess the credibility and character required to earn customers' confidence over time.
Be capable of transforming an initial contact into a long-term business partnership.

In the Nordic business culture, trust is often the primary factor behind purchasing decisions. We therefore place exceptional importance on integrity, credibility and relationship-building skills.
Other
Danieli - Morgårdshammar and the Danieli Group are already well known throughout the Nordic metals industry. Significant efforts have been made in recent years to increase our presence within production facilities, establish direct contacts with key stakeholders and strengthen our reputation across the region.
Several customers already work with Danieli. However, substantial opportunities remain to deepen those relationships and expand our involvement far beyond our current level of business.
Your mission will be to transform existing awareness into trust, and trust into long-term partnerships, customer loyalty and sustainable business growth.
We are looking for someone who can become the person our customers call first when they need advice, support or a reliable partner.
The successful candidate will not operate as a stand-alone salesperson.
Commercial strategy, customer development plans and growth initiatives are defined in close coordination with the Danieli Group headquarters in Italy and the Nordic Area.
The role is fully integrated within a broader international organization and supported by dedicated technical, commercial and engineering resources worldwide.
Daily support is provided by the Nordic Area Manager, while customer visits and business development activities are frequently performed jointly with Product Line Managers, technical specialists and senior representatives from Danieli headquarters.
The objective is to combine local presence and relationship-building with the engineering expertise, product knowledge and global resources of the Danieli Group. We are therefore looking for a person who enjoys being on the front line with customers, while being fully supported by an international team behind them.
You are not expected to be a lone hunter searching for orders.
We are looking for someone who can walk into a plant, understand the challenges faced by its people, speak their language and ultimately become the person they trust when it is time to place an order.
In the Nordic industrial culture, trust is not a sales tool, It is the foundation upon which long-term business is built.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position may be filled before the closing date. Interviews are conducted continuously throughout the recruitment process. Preferred start date is as soon as possible, but this is not a requirement.
Morgårdshammar AB is a member of Teknikföretagen and applies the relevant collective bargaining agreements within the Swedish engineering industry, including the Technology Agreement (Teknikavtalet).

Company description:
This is the Volvo Group Graduate ProgramA new era of manufacturing and R&D is here. Are you passionate about technology, eager to solve real business challenges, ready to drive innovation, and join our transformation journey? Then this Graduate program is for you!As part of the Graduate Program at Volvo Group, you will tackle real challenges from day one and contribute to the development of next-generation production solutions.The 15-month Graduate Program combines 50% time in your home department with 50% dedicated program activities, giving you broad exposure across Volvo Group. Through local and international rotations, short-term assignments and targeted training in areas such as operations, engineering and purchasing, you will build a strong understanding of our business, brands and strategy.
Job description:  Your future teamService Operations & Technology (SOT) is the engine behind customer uptime and service growth in the Volvo Group. Within the Trucks Technology & Industrial Division (TTI), we bring together engineering, purchasing, logistics, remanufacturing and technology into one global end-to-end organization. We are more than 5,000 colleagues across 50+ sites worldwide and we work close to our customers and markets to deliver reliable, high-performance service solutions that keep vehicles and machines running. 
 In our region Gent&Eu within SOT, we operate the Inbound and Outbound service market flows of spare parts. Our team is responsible for the Inbound flow, from order call-offs to our material suppliers through to arrival at the central distribution center. We work cross-functionally with all the great team members in the inbound supply chain. Our daily collaboration covers suppliers, operational planning, purchasing, engineering, remanufacturing and the central distribution center. We believe that the best results are achieved together, while having fun! Are you like us and want to join the journey to secure high customer satisfaction? Then this might be just the perfect role for you.
 How you’ll contributeThe aim of your role is to ensure that we continuously develop our Supply Chain in line with the Volvo Group ambitions. You will, among others, lead and coordinate cross-functional improvement initiatives, create structure, alignment and momentum across stakeholders.You will facilitate workshops, working groups and knowledge-sharing forums where different perspectives are brought together. Also, you will practice leadership through influence by clarifying objectives, engaging others, following up on commitments and supporting change. Our sites and operational work lie across Europe and as you will be located in Gothenburg Sweden, traveling within Europe will occasionally be required.
 Who are you?We are looking for someone with a strong transformation and collaborative mindset who is eager to learn, explore and understand the business. You thrive in dynamic environments, embrace new challenges and ambiguity and take ownership of your own development and growth.
 With strong analytical skills, you take initiative and drive tasks forward with determination while bringing fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to the team. You enjoy building relationships and leveraging a global network to create impact while working collaboratively across teams and functions. In addition, you contribute to a culture of continuous learning by actively sharing knowledge, exchanging insights and supporting the development of others.As this is a graduate position, we value your potential, learning agility and motivation to grow. We are interested in candidates who see leadership as part of their future career. What matters to us is your curiosity about how data, automation and digital solutions can improve the way we work and create lasting business value. We want you to be part of exploring and shaping what comes next.
 To qualify for the Graduate program
  You have completed a bachelor or master’s degree prior to the start of the program but not more than three years ago
 Should not have more than three years' full-time relevant working experience in the field prior to starting, excluding part-time work during studies
 Have relevant education within Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering or project management is required
 You have experience in Supply Chain-related work, such as logistics and warehousing, production, project management and understanding of data, system and application
 You are fluent in English, both written and verbal
 You are willing to travel and participate in international short-term assignments
  
Additional desirable skills
  Fluent in Swedish and Flemish
  
What’s in it for you?Our Volvo Group Graduate Program starts in August 2027 and you will be offered a permanent position at Volvo TTI SOT Gent&Eu with placement in Sweden, Gothenburg.
 These are some of the benefits of joining our program:
  An opportunity to work with the latest technology.
 An exciting and global working environment with experienced colleagues.
 Possibility to gain international experience through a short-term assignment abroad.
 A competitive salary and a permanent position from day one.
 Various workshops and seminars designed to help you grow into your future career at Volvo Group.
 The possibility to shape your own career with endless career opportunities.
  
The application processThe journey begins! An email confirmation will be sent when you submit your application. After this, it is still possible to update your personal profile by logging into your account. The hiring team will review your application together with the hiring manager. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted with information about the following steps.
 Last day to apply: 22nd of November 2026 
  As part of the recruitment process, a background check as well as alcohol and drug testing may be conducted. You will be informed if applicable.

Welcome to SSC Space (formerly Swedish Space Corporation), the perfect workplace for those passionate about technology in general and space in particular. 
With space organizations, research institutes, institutional and commercial actors as customers, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications, spacecraft consulting services, rocket and balloon systems, and much more. 
SSC Space also has one of the world’s largest global networks of ground stations for satellite communications. We own and operate the Esrange Space Center in Kiruna, northern Sweden, with the aim of launching satellites in the near future. 
Are you fueled by a passion for people and the ambition to create an awesome workplace? Are you ready to embark on an exciting journey with us to help Earth benefit from space? 
If you answer yes to these questions, we invite you to seize the opportunity to make a significant impact as optical communications engineer in our team. We are looking for a dedicated person who shares our core values of Customer passion, Care, Collaboration, Curiosity, and Courage. 
As an Optical Communications Engineer you will join our multidisciplinary optical team and contribute to developing satellite data services based on free-space optical communications. You will support system development, integration, testing and operational deployment, working across ground stations, spacecraft interfaces and customer missions.

REQUIREMENTS
MSc (or equivalent background) in aerospace engineering, engineering physics, electrical engineering, optical communications or a related field.
Experience in system engineering methods (requirements, interfaces, verification) and end-to-end system thinking. 
Ability to perform system-level analysis, requirements analysis and trade-offs.
Proven ability for problem solving, working with conflicting deadlines both individually and in a team environment to achieve program goals, with ability to prioritise work and deliver clear documentation (such as technical reports) on time. 
Fluency in English, both written and spoken.
Applicants must be legally allowed to work in the EU and hold a European citizenship. Swedish citizenship is an advantage. Evidence of eligibility will be required from candidates as part of the recruitment process.

In addition, experience with free-space optical communication systems, space systems and ground segment architectures, as well as RF or optical link budget and performance analysis is highly beneficial. Knowledge of network protocols and distributed system architectures is also considered an advantage. You should be able to work effectively both independently and in collaboration with others.

RESPONSIBILITIES
In your role as Optical Communications Engineer you are responsible for supporting the development, integration, and demonstration of SSC Space’s optical ground network services, contributing to both operational deployment and future service development. You operate within the Optical Program and support ongoing projects such as demonstration missions, ground station development, and network integration, while also exploring new applications such as deep-space optical communications and quantum technologies and providing technical support to the business developments. 
The main responsibilities include performing in-depth technical analyses of optical communication systems, including link performance and operational requirements, site surveys and environmental assessments, orbit analysis and mission geometry, end-to-end system and subsystem testing and network integration.  
The role also entails collaboration and interactions with internal and external partners and participation in technical discussions, workshops and project meetings, as well as on-site work of the SSC Space optical ground stations at the OGS sites (e.g. Australia and Chile) on occasion. Documentation and reporting of the work, tests and outcome are a part of the general responsibilities of the role.

BENEFITS
We offer you 
A unique opportunity to contribute to a wide range of projects and play an active role in both the Swedish and international space industry.
An excellent opportunity for personal and career development.
An exciting, international workplace characterized by an open atmosphere and proud employees all over the world. 

Additional benefits 
In addition to vacation and traditional public holidays, we offer extra paid leave throughout the year, such as time off between Christmas and New Year, Ascension Day, amounting to 6-11 extra days depending on the calendar. 
Wellness allowance of SEK 5,000 per year.
Health benefits such as voluntary health insurance and regular health checks for eligible employees. 
Access to a benefit bike through a tax-efficient leasing program.
Support for employee-driven activities that promote connection, health, and culture across teams.
Collective Agreement, including good pensions plans, parental pay and insurance.

 
LOCATION
This is a full-time, permanent position based at our office in Solna. 

NEXT STEP 
If this opportunity sparks your interest, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible! We review applications continuously and will conduct interviews throughout the process. 
When applying, please include your CV. While you are welcome to include a brief personal note or letter, our evaluation will primarily focus on your skills and qualifications as outlined in your CV, ensuring a fair and unbiased recruitment process. 
As part of our recruitment process, all candidates selected for employment undergo a background check and security screening. 
 
WE HELP EARTH BENEFIT FROM SPACE
SSC Space is a leading global provider of advanced space services, with more than 50 years of experience. We help space organizations, research institutes, commercial and institutional actors from all over the world to get access to space. 
With local presence on all continents and about 800 committed employees, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications and satellite control services, spacecraft operations, rocket and balloon systems, launch services and flight test services, as well as engineering, operations and consultancy services for space missions. 
 We help Earth benefit from Space. Learn more at sscspace.com

We are looking for an experienced AI Backend Engineer to build the core intelligence layer of a fast-scaling AI company backed by NVIDIA, Microsoft, and AWS.
About Antrino
Antrino Labs is building the platform that makes every square meter intelligent.
The physical world runs on processes nobody can actually see. Goods move, machines idle, space goes unused, and decisions about all of it are based on samples, guesses, and reports written after the fact. Antrino lets any organization deploy vision intelligence into a physical space and get back what is actually happening there, as structured, real-time information it can act on. Not a research project or a custom integration, but a platform where you describe what matters and deploy it.
We have grown from 6 people to a team of 28 in less than a year, closed our Seed round, announced together with Dagens Industri, and are registered with Inspektionen för strategiska produkter (ISP), the Swedish authority for strategic and dual-use products. Everything we build follows Privacy by Design.
The role
You will build the services that turn a customer's intent into working intelligence.
When a customer builds something in Studio, our composition canvas, that graph has to become a running system: a plan that decides which models to call, in what order, gated by cost and confidence, and that produces events and evidence a customer can trust. You will work on the compiler that turns the graph into an execution plan, the runtime that executes it, and the Python and TypeScript services that detection, classification, and measurement run through.
You will also work on our Agent, which interviews customers, proposes and edits these graphs, and deploys them with confirmation. Getting an LLM to reliably manipulate a structured graph, validate it, and explain its reasoning is a real engineering problem, not a prompting exercise.
The role sits between the team building our first-party detection models and the engineers building the product interface. It is backend systems engineering for a product whose core logic is built out of AI calls.
What you will work on
Backend services for detection, classification, and measurement, largely in Python with FastAPI
The compiler that turns a Studio graph into an execution plan, and the runtime that deploys and runs it
Routing logic that decides which model handles which work, including cost gating where a cheap model decides when an expensive one runs
The Agent's interview, graph-editing, and deployment flows that turn natural language into a working pipeline
Integrating our first-party detection models, and frontier model APIs where they do something ours do not yet, behind one clean interface
Turning raw model output into structured, auditable events and evidence an operator can trust
APIs and data models for streams, behaviors, runs, and events in PostgreSQL with row-level security
Tests and evaluation harnesses for logic that includes non-deterministic model calls
Debugging production issues that span a customer request, our orchestration, and the model call underneath

Our stack
You do not need experience with all of this, but you should recognize most of it and be able to argue about it.
Backend: Python, FastAPI, TypeScript, Node.jsData: PostgreSQL through Supabase, with row-level security, 
Streaming: RTSP ingestion, RTSP→HLS conversion, live and archive pipelines
Infrastructure: Azure, GitHub Actions, on-site compute reached over Tailscale
Who we are looking for Substantial backend experience on production systems, ideally where an LLM or ML model was part of the core logic rather than a bolted-on feature
Strong Python, and comfort in TypeScript or Node.js
Real experience designing APIs, data models, and service boundaries, including PostgreSQL
Experience building with LLM APIs beyond a chat wrapper: tool use, structured output, agentic flows, or a model as one step in a larger pipeline
An understanding of how to test systems with non-deterministic components
Experience with real-time or streaming data is a strong advantage
Excellent written and spoken English. Swedish is a plus, not a requirement

You can reason about a graph or compiler-shaped problem even if you have never built a compiler. You make decisions with incomplete information, take responsibility for the outcome, and say so clearly when something you built was wrong.
Life at Antrino
You will join a team of driven, ambitious people who thrive at a fast pace and enjoy working together. We go to AI events, host our own, and end plenty of weeks with an afterwork. You will work closely with our engineers in Stockholm and our growing team in Bangalore.
What we offer
Direct access to the founders, the engineering team, and customers
Real ownership of a core layer of the platform rather than delegated tickets
Potential participation in our stock option programme after the probationary period
Hardware of your choice
AI events, afterworks, team activities, and travel when the business requires it
Occupational pension, insurance, and friskvårdsbidrag

Process
Introductory conversation about your background and the role
Technical conversation about systems you have built and why you made the decisions you made. No whiteboard algorithm puzzles
Working session with the engineering team on a real problem from our stack
Conversation with the founders about options and terms

We review applications continuously. References may be requested at the final stage.
Apply with your CV and, if you have one, a link to something you have built. A repository, a shipped product, or a short note about a system you are proud of tells us more than a cover letter

Looking for a flexible part-time job alongside your studies or other commitments? Do you enjoy helping people, keeping things organized, and making a workplace feel welcoming? Then this might be the perfect role for you!
We're looking for a friendly and proactive Office Manager to take care of our Framna office in central Östersund.
Become part of the team
At Framna, we create digital products used by millions of people every day. But great products start with great people, and we believe a welcoming and well-functioning workplace makes all the difference.
Our Östersund office is home to a creative bunch of colleagues working with technology, design, and digital products. We also share our space with other companies, so there's always a mix of people around.
As our part-time Office Manager, you'll be the go-to person for the little (and sometimes bigger) things that keep the office running smoothly. You'll work independently in Östersund, with support from our Office and People team in Stockholm and Kalmar.
This is a 20% position, making it a great opportunity to combine with university studies or other commitments. We'll agree on a schedule together that works for both you and the needs of the office, giving you flexibility in how you spread your hours throughout the week. And if you're a student, you're more than welcome to stay and study at our office when you're not working!
What you will do
Your main mission is simple: make sure our office is a great place to be!
Some days you'll be making sure we have everything we need, other days you'll be helping organize an event or solving an unexpected office issue.
More specifically, you will be:

Making sure everyday office essentials are in place, from coffee and milk to printer supplies and other necessities.

Keeping the office welcoming, organized, and running smoothly, including taking care of plants and shared spaces.

Being the main contact person for our tenants and helping with practical questions and requests.

Coordinating with external suppliers and partners, such as cleaning services and property management.

Handling practical office administration, including access systems and coordinating checks of safety equipment.

Helping plan and organize local events, breakfasts, afterworks, and other fun activities.

Working closely with colleagues in Östersund and our Office team in other Framna studios.

Who you are
You don't need years of experience or an impressive CV to succeed in this role. What matters most to us is your attitude, your ability to take initiative, and your willingness to help others.
We believe you might feel at home with us if you:

Are friendly, service-minded, and enjoy making other people's day a little easier.

Are organized, reliable, and good at noticing what needs to be done.

Like taking initiative and finding practical solutions.

Feel comfortable working independently while staying connected with colleagues.

Enjoy meeting different people and creating a welcoming atmosphere.

Communicate comfortably in both Swedish and English.

Previous experience in service, administration, hospitality, or a similar role is a plus
Whether you're a university student looking for a flexible job or simply someone who enjoys making things run smoothly, we'd love to hear from you!
About Framna 
Framna means ‘to bring forward’ in Old Norse. And that is exactly what we do. We partner with industry leaders (and those about to be) to create excellent digital products that define markets, reshape industries, and deliver meaningful impact.
Born from the union of digital agencies Bontouch, Move, and Shape, Framna emerged from a strong, product-led culture. Today, over 600 of us collaborate across 11 studios in Denmark, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, Switzerland, and the US.
Every day, millions of users around the world rely on the products we help shape. From seamless payments to daily commutes, from better health management to smarter shopping. Our work supports more than €150 million in daily transactions and consistently earns an average App Store rating of 4.5.
Together with some of the world’s most ambitious brands, including Essity, SJ, Swish, SEB, and Vattenfall, we craft products that lead markets and push boundaries. Because when products win, businesses win. We call it Win by product.
What you get 
A flexible part-time role. We'll agree on a schedule together, making it easier to combine work with studies or other commitments.

An office to call your own. A welcoming workplace in central Östersund, where you're also welcome to stay and study outside your working hours.

A chance to make a difference. You'll play an important part in making everyday office life easier and more enjoyable for everyone.

Great colleagues. Friendly, creative people who enjoy spending time together and helping each other out.

Freedom and responsibility. We trust you to take initiative, organize your work, and find smart ways to make things run smoothly.

Our hiring process
We like to keep things simple:

Short introductory call

Interview

Reference check

The position is based at our office in Östersund, Sweden. This is an on-site role, with working hours planned together based on the needs of the office and your availability.
We're reviewing applications on a rolling basis, so don't wait to apply. We look forward to learning more about you!

Lyten is leading an industrial revolution through Lyten 3D Graphene™, a breakthrough supermaterial unlocking a new generation of products — from lithium–sulfur batteries and energy storage systems to concrete admixtures, lightweight composites, and next-generation sensors that are revolutionizing industries. Together, these innovations are making a massive global improvement and driving real-world impact across energy, mobility, construction, and defense.
At Lyten, we believe the most meaningful careers begin with purpose — and with people who want to make a difference. We’re not just developing advanced supermaterials — we’re about to change the world as we know it, reshaping how energy is stored, how products are built, and how progress is made.
We’re entering an exciting growth phase, scaling production across the U.S. and Europe and expanding our team of engineers, scientists, and innovators.

Director of Manufacturing Engineering
Job Scope
As Director of Manufacturing Engineering, you will lead and grow the team responsible for developing and industrialising the manufacturing solutions required for Lyten's next-generation battery technologies. You will play a key role in bridging technology development and industrial execution, ensuring future products can be successfully scaled into robust, efficient, and high-quality manufacturing processes.
This is a strategic leadership role with significant influence on technology decisions, industrialisation strategy, manufacturing concepts, and future production capabilities. A key focus will be on growing the organisation while working closely with R&D, Product Development, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and external partners to build the manufacturing platform that supports Lyten's future growth.
By helping transform breakthrough technologies into scalable manufacturing solutions, you will play a direct role in enabling the energy transition and strengthening Europe's industrial future.

Key Responsibilities
· Lead, develop, and grow the Manufacturing Engineering organisation.
· Build a high-performing culture with clear roles, responsibilities, and ways of working.
· Drive the industrialisation of next-generation products, processes, and manufacturing technologies.
· Collaborate with R&D, Product Development, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturing readiness.
· Shape manufacturing strategy, technology roadmaps, and future production capabilities.
· Evaluate and implement new manufacturing concepts, automation solutions, and production technologies.
· Drive operational excellence, continuous improvement, and long-term capability development.
· Build strong relationships with suppliers, partners, and key stakeholders.
Requirements
· Degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.
· Extensive experience within manufacturing engineering, industrialisation, production engineering, or advanced manufacturing.
· Proven leadership experience building, developing, and leading engineering organisations.
· Strong track record of scaling manufacturing operations and industrialising new products, technologies, or manufacturing concepts.
· Experience leading managers, engineers, and multidisciplinary teams in complex environments.
· Background from automotive, industrial equipment, electronics, battery, or other advanced manufacturing industries.
· Strong strategic mindset combined with the ability to execute and deliver results.
· Experience working across international and cross-functional organisations.
· Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.
· Fluent in English, written and spoken.
Who You Are

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral fellow in Structural studies of mitochondrial DNA replication
jobs.description:
This postdoctoral position is part of a research project funded by a Wallenberg Scholar grant. The postdoctoral researcher will work in an interdisciplinary team with expertise in molecular biology, biochemistry and structural biology. The project aims to understand the molecular mechanisms that govern mitochondrial DNA replication and gene expression, and how defects in these processes contribute to human disease.
 
Subject area 
Structural studies of mitochondrial DNA replication
 
Subject area description 
Mitochondrial DNA replication is essential for maintaining mtDNA integrity and stability and thereby for normal mitochondrial function and cellular energy production. Defects in the replication process can lead to mtDNA depletion or deletions and cause mitochondrial disease.
Our research aims to understand the molecular mechanisms that govern replication of human mtDNA. We combine structural biology, in vitro biochemistry and cell biology to investigate how the mitochondrial DNA replication machinery is organized and regulated. A particular focus is on structural and functional studies of the protein complexes involved in mtDNA replication and on understanding how disease-associated mutations affect these processes.
 
Job assignments
In this project, In this project, the postdoctoral researcher will carry out structural and functional studies of protein and protein-DNA complexes involved in mitochondrial DNA replication. A central aim will be to determine structures of replication complexes using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and use these structures to understand how the proteins interact and regulate mtDNA replication at the molecular level.
The work will include preparation and biochemical characterization of protein complexes, cryo-EM sample preparation and grid optimization, as well as processing and structural analysis of cryo-EM data. Structural findings will be combined with in vitro biochemical analyses to test mechanistic models and investigate how disease-associated mutations affect the function of the replication machinery.
The postdoctoral researcher is expected to drive the project independently while working closely with other members of the research group and our collaborators.
 
Eligibility 
The eligibility criteria for employing teaching staff are set out in Chapter 4 of the Higher Education Ordinance and in the Appointment Procedure for Teaching Posts at the University of Gothenburg.
To be eligible for appointment as a postdoc, the applicant is required to have a doctoral degree, a doctoral degree in art or a foreign degree that is deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree. This eligibility requirement must be met before the employment decision is made.
In the first instance, those who have completed their degree no more than three years prior to the end of the application period shall be considered. Those who have completed their degree more than three years prior to the end of the application period may also be considered in the first instance if special grounds exist. Special grounds relate to leave of absence due to illness, parental leave, commissions of trust within union organisations, service within the defence services or other similar circumstances, as well as clinical service or service/assignment relevant to the subject area. 
 
Assessment criteria 
We are seeking a highly motivated researcher with a doctoral degree in structural biology, biochemistry, molecular biology or a related field.
Documented experience in structural studies of proteins or macromolecular complexes using cryo-electron microscopy is required. Experience in protein purification and protein biochemistry is also required.
Experience in single-particle cryo-EM, including sample preparation, grid optimization, data processing and structural analysis, is particularly meritorious. Experience in structural studies of protein-DNA complexes is a strong advantage. Knowledge of mitochondrial systems and experience in cloning, mutagenesis, protein expression, cell culture and in vitro biochemical analyses are considered merits.
Great emphasis will be placed on scientific skills and the ability to independently plan, carry out and analyse research. The work involves close collaboration both within and outside the research group, making good teamwork and communication skills important. The candidate is expected to have strong scientific curiosity and the ability to work both independently and as part of an interdisciplinary team.
Excellent spoken and written English is required, as the research group operates in an international environment.
 
Regulations for the evaluation of qualifications for academic positions are given in Chapter 4, Section 3 - 4 of the Higher Education Ordinance.
 
Employment 
The employment is full time and temporary, two years with the possibility of one year's extension, with placement at the Institute of Biomedicine. First day of employment as agreed.

Connect platform development to the wider business context and ensure investments create meaningful value for Husqvarna Group.
